recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if O&O reopens the broader NutritionOrder cardinality/modeling question; directly restoring old DSTU1 EnteralFormula 0..* wording would conflict with the historical application and later administration modeling.
issue_request: FHIR-3996 is a Published FHIR-core/O&O change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It requested removing NutritionOrder.item and moving schedule/timing semantics into OralDiet, Supplement, and EnteralFormula so the separate diet, supplement, and enteral order components were not hidden behind a shared item wrapper.
initial_application: The historical application is in old spreadsheet source. Commit 7d67ca802e5a4a4a472dcba2a975d3e1b6b9a230 marked NutritionOrder.item, NutritionOrder.item.scheduled[x], and NutritionOrder.item.isInEffect inactive, moved item child structures up to NutritionOrder.oralDiet, NutritionOrder.supplement, and NutritionOrder.enteralFormula, and added #3996 notes to the new per-type scheduled elements. Later source conversions preserved that shape, and commit 1a5062f0a41dca024be7fb527908dcec638166f8 refined schedule backbones into explicit schedule.timing/asNeeded structures.
additional_context: NutritionOrder is active in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition has no NutritionOrder.item path, defines oralDiet.schedule.timing and supplement.schedule.timing, and places repeatable enteral quantity/rate/schedule details under enteralFormula.administration. The Jira resolution text's apparent EnteralFormula 0..* wording should not be replayed literally: the original #3996 source application already left enteralFormula as 0..1, and later Published issues FHIR-6100 and FHIR-6101 moved repeatable enteral feeding detail into enteralFormula.administration 0..*. Community searches found no conflicting FHIR-3996 discussion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source hunk was necessary because the current authoritative source already implements the applied item removal and later enteral scheduling decisions.

related_jiras.note: Published later enteral feeding decision that created repeatable NutritionOrder.enteralFormula.administration with quantity, rate, and schedule.
Published later issue to move enteral formula scheduling next to quantity; its disposition points to FHIR-6100 and explains the current schedule location.
